page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the ARM64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz using ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processors with one thread per core. The instance provides 128 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB per core. The cache structure consists of 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and an 80 MB shared L3 cache. Cryptographic operations are supported via hardware-level AES instructions. This server configuration does not include local storage, complimentary public IPv4 addresses, or dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark testing demonstrates high throughput across data-intensive and memory-bound operations. The instance achieved top-tier rankings in Geekbench multi-core performance (22,619.0), PassMark memory testing (3,269.65), and PassMark database operations (49,533.61). Memory bandwidth benchmarks place the system in the top 25%, with cached reads reaching 3,959.51 GB/sec and uncached sequential reads measuring 343.0 GB/sec. Application testing shows strong results in Redis SET throughput at 68.8 million operations per second, static web serving at 76.05 GB/sec, Clang compilation, and decompression. CPU-intensive operations in stress-ng and PassMark extended instruction suites remain in the average tier.

The 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation provides predictable CPU performance without simultaneous multithreading overhead. However, the lack of bundled local NVMe storage requires external persistent storage over the network, and the absence of x86 vector extensions (AVX, AVX-512, AMX) restricts software compatibility to native ARM64 ecosystems. The instance is suited for multi-threaded compilation pipelines, Redis caching clusters, high-concurrency web serving, and distributed database nodes.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-32 is an ARM64 general-purpose instance powered by 32 dedicated Neoverse-V2 physical cores at 3.0 GHz and 128 GB of RAM. Lacking bundled local storage and GPU accelerators, it allocates 4.0 GB of memory per dedicated thread. Benchmarks show top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core metrics and PassMark memory and database evaluations, along with strong memory bandwidth reaching 343.0 GB/sec on uncached reads. Real-world application benchmarks demonstrate high throughput for Redis caching at 68.8 million operations per second and static web serving at 76.05 GB/sec. Operating purely on dedicated ARMv8 architecture without simultaneous multithreading or x86 instruction sets, c4a-standard-32 delivers predictable performance suited for distributed databases, caching tiers, software compilation pipelines, and containerized backend workloads.
